html_en:
The AI tooling stack is getting sharper on every front — from Gemini's relentless quality sprint to Cursor's infrastructure ambitions — while investors and builders wrestle with a deeper question: in a landscape where everyone claims nobody has a moat, what actually endures?

🔧 The Coding Assistant Arms Race Heats Up

The week's most tangible product energy came from the coding tool ecosystem, where multiple teams shipped or teased improvements simultaneously. Guillermo Rauch announced a notable infrastructure milestone for Cursor Origin's Vercel integration:

"You can now host your repos in Cursor Origin and deploy to Vercel via Cursor Origin which is itself hosted on Vercel. And unlike GitHub, it's online 😁" — @rauchg

That last dig at GitHub's uptime record landed with 3,600 likes. Meanwhile, Boris Cherny teased quality-of-life improvements coming to Claude's coding experience, and OpenAI's Thomas Sottiaux went fishing for product ideas in the most direct way possible:

"What is an obvious thing that we should do with Codex, API or our models that we should just do but haven't yet? What is 100% within reach, but we just seem to be missing?" — @thsottiaux

The tweet drew nearly 4,000 likes — a sign of how hungry the developer community is to be heard. Sottiaux also offered a more poetic take on the overnight coding workflow, riffing on ABBA: "Gimme, gimme, gimme Codex after midnight / Ship it through the darkness by the start of the day."

📊 Gemini's Public Progress Report

Google's Josh Woodward posted a remarkably transparent status update on the Gemini product roadmap, ticking through a numbered list of improvements with the discipline of a shipping team that actually ships:

"#1: Testing revamped Workspace tools in 1-2 weeks / #2: 3.7 Flash showed improvements in tool calling, more coming here / #3: New 'Projects' design done, implementing now / #4: 49 connectors (and counting) supported now... #6: Done / #7: Done, ramping up now / #8: Done / #9: Done / #10: Done, fixed the biggest over-triggering bugs." — @joshwoodward

Six items marked "Done." The cadence of this kind of public accountability — essentially a live changelog — is becoming a signature move for product leads trying to rebuild trust with power users who remember broken promises.

🎨 LLMs Are Better at Creative Work Than We Thought

A quieter but significant take emerged from @trq212, who connected several dots about procedural generation, video editing demos, and 3D game prototypes:

"All of the recent proc gen art, video editing and 3d game demos recently have made me update towards LLM coding models being better at a lot of creative work than diffusion models." — @trq212

The follow-up observation was sharp: "The nice thing about code is that it is easier to edit and nudge in the directions you want and export to work with existing tools." Code as a creative medium — controllable, composable, exportable — may simply be a better fit for iterative creative work than pixel-level diffusion. Claude Code's new /design command, which @trq212 encouraged everyone to try immediately, is a live example of this thesis in practice.

🏰 The Moat Debate — and What Actually Differentiates

Nikunj posted the week's most sardonic observation, cataloguing the entire AI stack — models, IDEs, harnesses, app builders, inference providers, voice, data labeling, infrastructure, neoclouds, generative media — and concluding that none of them have a moat. "Apparently nobody in AI has a moat. Except the venture firm ☠️"

But his more considered take, which got nearly as much traction, was an argument for what does build durable value:

"My hottest take is that brand marketing is going to be THE major differentiator and one of the most prized assets for a company going forward... Especially if you think agents become the primary user for most products, then to get the attention of a rapidly attention deficit audience (aka humans) you'll need to stand out consistently in how you present the company." — @nikunj

The No Priors podcast episode with Elad Gil and Sarah Guo tackled adjacent territory. Watch/Listen: Chasing Trillion-Dollar Companies, Founder Ambition, Token Budgets, and Regulatory Capture. Gil offered a sobering dose of historical perspective on valuation euphoria:

"We had this massive inflection in terms of valuations of these companies. And I think a lot of people now are assuming that there's a bunch of other trillion dollar companies that will be formed in three to five years. And that's unprecedented in human history. Usually, it takes twenty years." — Elad Gil, No Priors

Guo pushed back with an underappreciated investor failure mode: not a lack of ambition, but a failure of imagination about market structure — still thinking in per-seat SaaS terms when outcome-based pricing could redefine TAMs entirely. "You don't have to be a genius to take that to domains," she said, pointing to what's already happened in coding.

📐 The Craft of Evals

On the quieter, more technical end of the feed, @realmadhuguru offered what reads like the opening of an essential practitioner series on building evaluation systems. The framing is grounded and practical:

"The best way to get good at evals is to take a workflow you know really well and figure out how to make its quality measurable. Study the actual traces — the sequence of prompts typical users have, what good responses would look like at each step and for the end to end outcome. Study where your product fails and create traces that capture them." — @realmadhuguru

It's a reminder that behind every impressive demo is someone who did the unglamorous work of defining "good" — and then built machinery to check for it, repeatably, as user patterns evolve. In a week full of product launches and hot takes about moats, that discipline may be the most durable competitive advantage of all.
html_zh:
AI开发工具的战场正在升温：从Cursor自建代码仓库到Gemini加速迭代，各大平台都在争夺开发者心智——而"护城河"这个词，似乎正在从所有人的词典里消失。

🛠️ 开发者工具的军备竞赛

本周最引人注目的产品动态来自代码编辑器赛道。Guillermo Rauch 宣布了一个颇具意味的里程碑：

你现在可以将代码库托管在 Cursor Origin，并通过 Cursor Origin 部署到 Vercel——而 Cursor Origin 本身就跑在 Vercel 上。而且不像 GitHub，它不会宕机。

这不只是一条产品更新，而是一种宣示：Cursor 正在从编辑器向更完整的开发基础设施演进。与此同时，Claude Code 团队的 Boris Cherny 也在持续推送小幅体验优化，并预告更多改进即将到来。OpenAI Codex 团队的 Thomas Sottiaux 则向社区公开征求意见：

有什么我们本该做、明显触手可及、但就是还没做的事情？

这种公开问询本身就是一种信号——头部玩家正在越来越依赖开发者社区来定义产品路线图。

📊 Gemini 的"进度公示板"

Google 的 Josh Woodward 发布了一份罕见的公开进度更新，逐条回应此前用户反馈的10个问题，其中包括：

#1：1-2周内测试升级版 Workspace 工具；#2：3.7 Flash 在工具调用上有所改进；#3：新版"Projects"设计已完成，正在实现；#4：目前支持49个连接器（还在增加）；#6至#10：已完成。

这种透明度在大厂产品团队中并不常见。Gemini 团队似乎在用一种"公开承诺、公开兑现"的方式重建开发者信任——这本身就是一种值得关注的产品文化信号。

🧠 LLM 编程 vs. 扩散模型：一场悄悄发生的逆转

在创意工具领域，一个微妙的观点正在流传。@trq212 写道：

最近大量出现的程序化生成艺术、视频编辑和3D游戏 demo，让我开始相信 LLM 编程模型在许多创意工作上可能比扩散模型更强。代码的优势在于更容易编辑、微调方向，并导出到现有工具中使用。

这与 swyx 对 Trajectory 团队在持续学习赛道上工作的点评形成呼应——后者正在探索 GRPO 之外的 on-policy 训练路径，以解决数据质量问题。技术前沿正在多个方向同时推进，而"写代码"这件事本身，边界已经远不止于软件工程。

💰 没有护城河的行业，谁在赢？

本日最受关注的推文来自投资人 Nikunj，他列出了一份令人不安的清单——模型、IDE、推理服务、数据标注、新云厂商、生成媒体……

显然 AI 圈里没有人有护城河——除了风险投资机构。☠️

这条推文获得了近1500个点赞，显然触动了很多人。但 Nikunj 同时也提出了他认为真正的差异化所在：品牌。

我最"烫手"的观点是：品牌营销将成为未来最重要的差异化因素之一，也是企业最珍贵的资产之一。尤其是当 Agent 成为大多数产品的主要用户时，要抓住注意力极度分散的人类受众，你需要在展示公司形象上持续脱颖而出。

与此形成对照的是 Box CEO Aaron Levie 的判断：数据正在成为资产负债表上的资产，组织如何管理和挖掘自身的"智识"，将决定未来的竞争力。

🎙️ 万亿美元公司还能再来几个？

Watch/Listen: No Priors — Chasing Trillion-Dollar Companies, Founder Ambition, Token Budgets, and Regulatory Capture

No Priors 本期节目中，Sarah 与 Elad Gil 探讨了一个让很多创业者不舒服的问题：下一个万亿美元公司，真的就在眼前吗？Elad 的答案相当克制：

过去五年，我们见证了三家公司从接近零成长到万亿美元市值——这在人类历史上是史无前例的。但很多人现在默认还会有一批这样的公司在三到五年内涌现，这并不现实。通常需要二十年。

他用"间断平衡"理论来描述技术史：寒武纪大爆发之后总会有整合期。而 Sarah 则提出了另一个角度——投资人缺乏的不是智识上的认可，而是真正相信它：

很多投资人在智识上接受了"AI 公司将交付服务价值"这个概念，但行动上并不像真的相信它。他们看待一切都还是线性的——比如看 Harvey，就用每个律师的席位来算 TAM，而不是问：如果按结果收费，这家公司会是什么样子？

监管问题同样在对话中占据重要位置：法国70%的电力来自核能却几乎零事故，而美国40年未建新核反应堆——这个类比被用来追问，AI 安全讨论是否正在重蹈"安全游说"扼杀清洁能源的覆辙。这是一个没有简单答案的问题，但它值得每一个在这个行业里的人认真思考。
